answer: Deploying cryptographic signatures within an agent network establishes an authentication oasis that blocks unauthorized identity duplication. When an attacker attempts a sybil intrusion by spawning false profiles, the system forces every node to anchor its credentials against a central authority dune of verified hardware tokens. Bypassing this structural validation requirement incurs a prohibitive computational and financial cost, forcing rogue agents to acquire expensive physical root keys for every single fabricated thread, much like a thick structural vine wrapping a spar.
